essence: Four outer strokes — half-open eyes, steady mind, nose-tip gaze, moon-sun dissolved — then the vision: light-form without exterior, one supreme person attained; after which speech ends.

sections.SUMMARY: Four outer strokes — half-open eyes, steady mind, nose-tip gaze, moon-sun dissolved — then the vision: light-form without exterior, one supreme person attained; after which speech ends.
sections.KEY TERMS:
* **ardhoddhāṭitalocana** — half-open-eyed
* **sthiramanas** — steady-minded
* **nāsāgradattekṣaṇa** — nose-tip gaze
* **candrārka** — moon-sun
* **trispandabhāva** — triple-throb state
* **jyotīrūpa** — light-form
* **pumāṃs** — person
* **vācya** — to be said
sections.LOCAL CONTEXT: Outer portrait, then vision, then silence.
sections.EXPLANATION: Outward portrait first: half-open eyes, steadied mind, gaze placed on the nose-tip — then moon and sun (candrārkau) too (api) attained dissolution (līnatām upagatau) in the interior (antare) of the triple-throb state (trispandabhāva): inhalation, exhalation and their juncture dissolved inward. Then the vision: light-formed (jyotīrūpam), devoid of all exteriority (aśeṣabāhyarahitam), and one (ekam), supreme (param) person (pumāṃsam) — reality (tattvam) attains (eti) that (tat) state (padam): the supreme thing (vastu paramam). Close: what (kim) more (adhikam) is to be said (vācyam) here (atra)? Showing complete, speech stops — the question is the period.
sections.BOUNDARY: Whether the triple-throb state (trispandabhāva) is breath or consciousness is unresolved.
sections.RELATED: * Anubhavanivedana v.3 — what sounds, postures, breathes.

rasa.justification: The sthāyibhāva is devotion (bhakti) in the mode of vision (darśana); the vyabhicāri is wonder (camatkāra) at the light-form person.
